executive_summary: First board under the new driver-window rule (drivers published on or after last_meeting.date unless weight >= 6). The candidate bytes hash to b6045fa6006e... on disk and under the shared canonical form, and canonical(data/current.json) gives the same hash; npm run check passes with zero structural flags, and the frontends and scripts are clean in the working tree. The pruning is correct: the 2026-10-28 candidate held exactly 21 drivers (16 Sep - 19 Oct, weights 2-4), none of which qualifies, so the rendered 'since 2026-10-28' header is now true. Primary sources check out. The federalreserve.gov statement (10-2 vote, Cook/Hammack for +1/4, 'expanding at a strong pace', 'Inflation remains elevated') matches. The press-conference PDF has 'real activity is clearly pointing in the right direction ... But inflation is too high', H1 GDP revised to 2.4%, Q3 'likely running above 3 percent', 'I don't believe in forward guidance absent exigent circumstances' and 'I also don't believe in prejudging meetings'. BEA PI&O Sep matches (PCE +0.5% m/m / 3.6% y/y, core +0.3% / 3.1%, real PCE <0.1%, real DPI -0.3%, saving 3.8%; Aug 3.4% / 3.0% from the 30 Sep release), and so does BEA Q3 GDP (3.4%, Q2 2.2%, final sales to private domestic purchasers 4.9%). The BoC release and opening statement also match (2.5%, Bank Rate 2.75%, deposit 2.45%, ~3.5% by year-end, 3% in 2027 a point above July, 2% mid-2028, 'proceed carefully', ex-gasoline 2.2%), and the Sep SEP shows 16 of 18 dots above 3.875 for end-2026. Pricing reproduces exactly. At 18:15 ET Kalshi showed Fed H25 0.73/0.74, H26 0.02/0.03, H0 0.23/0.24 and cuts 0/0.01, which normalise to 75.6/23.4/1.0, and BoC H25 0.36/0.38, H26 0/0.01, H0 0.62/0.64 and cuts 0/0.01, which normalise to 36.9/62.1/1.0. The as_of stamps are the real last trades (22:01:30Z @0.74, 19:07:35Z @0.37), the Polymarket legs recompute to 74.7/24.6/0.7 and 35.7/63.9/0.4 with $8.20M / $86k volume, and the implied rates are correct. Scores recompute to Fed +6 lean hike and BoC +3 hold, every breakdown sums to its weight, and same-URL pairs carry distinct facets. The calendar matches BLS (6 Nov, 10 Nov, 4 Dec), the StatCan Daily calendar (30 Oct GDP, 6 Nov LFS) and the 2026 PDF (CPI Oct on 16 Nov). Verdict REVISE on two majors, both in boc-h7, the largest BoC driver. (1) Its market_validation starts the Kalshi window at the post-release trough. The Dec 25bp-hike leg was 0.48/0.49 before 09:45 and traded 0.46 -> 0.33 within 12 minutes of the release that boc-h7 cites, so '0.33 -> 0.42' presents a partial rebound from a release-driven fall of 13 cents as hawkish confirmation; the leg is 0.37 now. (2) Its forecast says 'pre-meeting Kalshi/Polymarket ~96%', but Kalshi Oct H25 was 0.83/0.84 and Polymarket 85.3% at 09:08 ET; 96% was BlueGamma CORRA OIS. Operator instructions: (a) restate drivers.boc.hawkish[0].market_validation over the full window (pre-release ~0.48 -> 0.33 trough -> 0.42 at 13:00 -> 0.37 on 29 Oct) and either link the Bloomberg/Globe and Mail swaps figure or mark it 'via ... unverified'; (b) correct drivers.boc.hawkish[0].data.forecast to the venue numbers (Kalshi ~84%, Polymarket 85%; OIS ~96% labelled as OIS) and re-justify surprise=1 in the light of the market reaction to the same release, recomputing total_score.boc if the weight changes; (c) then re-freeze and resubmit. The minors are optional for this round.

findings.issue: boc-h7 uses only the rebound leg of the decision-day move as hawkish validation. The Kalshi December 25bp-hike leg fell sharply on the release boc-h7 itself cites (09:45 ET press release), and the quoted '0.33 -> 0.42 between the 10:00 and 13:00 ET hourly closes' starts at that release-driven trough. Over the whole window the market read the decision package as dovish for December (about 0.48 before the release, 0.37 on 29 Oct), the opposite sign to the +4 the driver contributes. The second leg, 'Bloomberg swaps ~60% ... (Globe and Mail, 28 Oct)', is an unlinked second-hand figure that is not labelled 'via' in this field. I could not locate it.
findings.evidence: Kalshi KXCBDECISIONCANADA-26DEC-H25 hourly candles (series/KXCBDECISIONCANADA/markets/.../candlesticks, period_interval=60, read 2026-10-29 18:16 ET): bid/ask 0.47/0.49 in the 08:00 and 09:00 ET candles with no trades, 0.48/0.49 through 27 Oct. Trades on /trade-api/v2/markets/trades for 28 Oct: 09:45:29 @0.46, 09:47:02 @0.42-0.43 (276 contracts), 09:48:45 @0.35, 09:57:11 @0.33, then 10:02:15 @0.39 and 10:19:15 @0.43. Candle close 0.33 at 10:00 and 0.42 at 13:00. Live book 0.36/0.38 on 29 Oct, last 19:07:35Z @0.37. Net change from pre-release to now is about -11c. The bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/ release time is 09:45 ET.

findings.issue: boc-h7 gives the wrong number for the pre-meeting probability and credits it to the wrong source. It reads '+25bp (pre-meeting Kalshi/Polymarket ~96%)', but on the morning of 28 Oct both venues priced the October hike at about 84-85%. The 96% was the BlueGamma CORRA OIS figure. The error understates how much of the hike was still open on the venues, and it feeds the driver's surprise=1 scoring.
findings.evidence: Kalshi KXCBDECISIONCANADA-26OCT-H25 hourly candles on 2026-10-28: close 0.86 (bid/ask 0.84/0.86) at 08:00 ET and 0.83 (0.83/0.84) at 09:00 ET; 26OCT-H0 0.14/0.15 at 09:00 ET. The prior candidate (git 2516384^:Rates_decisions/data/current.json, as_of 2026-10-28T09:13:57) has betting.boc[0] Polymarket hike 0.853 / hold 0.147 at 09:08:35 ET, and meetings.boc.pricing 'CORRA OIS-implied via BlueGamma' hike 0.96.

findings.issue: fed-h12 scores the Q3 GDP release as hawkish only and leaves out its price block, which was the day's clearest disinflation signal. Quarterly PCE inflation slowed to 2.1% SAAR from 5.0%, and core to 2.5% from 3.3%. fed-h11's title 'both re-accelerate' holds on year-on-year terms only. The 'no slack + above-target inflation' reasoning should acknowledge the quarterly deceleration.
findings.evidence: https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-3rd-quarter-2026 (read 2026-10-29 18:14 ET): 'The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, compared with an increase of 5.0 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, compared with an increase of 3.3 percent.'

findings.issue: fed-h11 credits the 08:00-09:00 ET Kalshi uptick to PCE alone, while fed-h12 says the same 08:30 move 'cannot be split between the two'. Over the full window the 08:30 data day was dovish on the market (0.78 -> 0.80 -> 0.75 -> 0.74), and the drivers dated 29 Oct net +3 hawkish. The text discloses the give-back, so this does not block, but the two drivers contradict each other on attribution.

Candidate drivers.fed.hawkish[3].market_validation reads 'unverified (released at the same 08:30 ET as PCE; Kalshi move cannot be split between the two)'.

findings.issue: fed-d7 puts 'going the right way' in quotation marks, but the transcript says 'inflation compensation is going in the right way' and, of expectations, 'They've gone the right way too'. The reason field also claims this driver is 'the main reason December is priced near 75%', while its own market_validation records the hike leg rising during the press conference. That causal claim has no evidence behind it.
findings.evidence: https://www.federalreserve.gov/mediacenter/files/FOMCpresconf20261028.pdf (pdftotext): 'Inflation compensation as measured by swaps prices, many other measures, inflation compensation is going in the right way ... They've gone the right way too.' The Kalshi 26DEC-H25 candle closes at 15:00 / 16:00 ET on 28 Oct are 0.80 and 0.81.

findings.issue: Part of boc-h8's wording cannot be found on the page it links. It cites the FAD press release, but 'slack absorbed by 2028' and the quoted 'less downward pressure on prices to offset these cost pressures' appear only in Macklem's opening statement. Both pages are on bankofcanada.ca, so the source rule holds, but the link does not support the quoted words.
findings.evidence: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/opening-statement-2026-10-28/ contains 'This absorbs the remaining slack in the economy' and 'there is less downward pressure on prices to offset these cost pressures'. https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/ (read 2026-10-29 18:14 ET) contains neither phrase.

findings.issue: Carried from the 2026-10-28 review (finding 6) and still open. The primary pricing block and the 'independent venue' are both event-contract ladders (Kalshi and Polymarket), so their agreement within about 1pp is weaker cross-validation than two different instruments would give. The only non-binary instrument, the BoC swaps figure of about 60%, is second-hand and points the other way.
